finding.title: Post-leave WebSocket room subscription TOCTOU race in welcome() and subscribe()
finding.description: In Gateway.welcome() (src/backend/messaging/presentation/messaging.socket.gateway.ts:555-588) and Gateway.subscribe() (messaging.socket.gateway.ts:502-510), room membership is queried asynchronously via listRooms.execute(connection.userId) or roomOfMember(this.deps.rooms, input.roomId, connection.userId) and then this.join(ws, roomId) is called without checking whether a concurrent membersChanged removal event (messaging.socket.gateway.ts:121-123) occurred while the query was in flight. Because SocketConnection.leave() (messaging.socket.connection.ts:65-67) only deletes from this.roomIds when roomId is already present, a removal emitted before join() is a no-op. When welcome() or subscribe() resumes, it calls this.join(ws, roomId) and this.presenceSnapshot(ws, roomId, ...), subscribing the departed user's socket to the Bun pub/sub topic room:<roomId> for the lifetime of the socket (which can be extended via auth.refresh). While E2EE key-epoch rotation prevents decrypting post-leave message ciphertexts, the departed user continues receiving real-time room metadata broadcasts (presence, typing, receipt, message.new metadata/ciphertext, room.rotated, sender-keys.available).
finding.root_cause: Gateway.welcome() (line 557) and Gateway.subscribe() (line 503) do not re-verify membership or check a membership-change version counter after awaiting async membership lookups (and subscribe() does not check connection.isReleased), while SocketConnection.leave() (messaging.socket.connection.ts:65-67) is a no-op if called before join().

trace.step: Gateway.subscribe() awaits roomOfMember() at line 503 (and Gateway.welcome() awaits listRooms.execute() at line 557), observing active membership in room R.

Concurrently, DELETE /api/rooms/:roomId/members/me commits the leave and emits events.membersChanged(room, { added: null, removed: actor }), which invokes Gateway.membersChanged() (messaging.socket.gateway.ts:121-123) and calls this.leave(ws, R).
SocketConnection.leave(R) returns false without recording the removal because this.roomIds does not yet contain R.

Gateway.subscribe() (line 508) or Gateway.welcome() (line 566) resumes and calls this.join(ws, R) and this.presenceSnapshot(ws, R, ...), subscribing the ex-member's socket to topic room:<R> and leaking future room metadata broadcasts.

finding.remediation: Track a monotonic membershipVersion counter on Gateway incremented in membersChanged() whenever removed !== null. Capture membershipVersion before awaiting listRooms.execute() in welcome() and roomOfMember() in subscribe(); after the await, abort if connection.isReleased is true, and if membershipVersion changed, re-query membership before calling this.join(ws, roomId).

lead.title: Podman pod publishes unauthenticated Valkey and default-credential PostgreSQL ports without loopback host binding
lead.description: scripts/pod.ts publishes ports 3001:3000, 5433:5432, and 6380:6379 without a 127.0.0.1: host bind prefix, binding 0.0.0.0 by default. chat-rsa-cache runs docker.io/valkey/valkey:9.2-alpine without requirepass and chat-rsa-db runs docker.io/library/postgres:18-alpine with static chat:chat credentials. On an untrusted network without a host firewall blocking TCP 5433 and 6380, a network peer can flush revoked-session:<sid> or rl:* keys in Valkey (reviving signed-out JWT sessions and bypassing rate limits) or access PostgreSQL directly.
lead.claimed_root_cause: scripts/pod.ts:44 omits 127.0.0.1: in -p port mappings while lines 47 and 51 start PostgreSQL with static chat:chat credentials and Valkey without authentication.

blockers.blocker: Actual host network exposure and firewall rules (nftables/ufw) when running scripts/pod.ts cannot be observed from source.

lead.validation_plan: While the pod is running, inspect `ss -tlnp '( sport = :5433 or sport = :6380 )'` and host firewall rules; if exposed on non-loopback interfaces, prefix `-p 127.0.0.1:${HOST_PORTS.database}:5432 -p 127.0.0.1:${HOST_PORTS.cache}:6379` in scripts/pod.ts:44.
